messages.text:
1.  Dus als ik het goed begrijp: mijn transactie zit straks al in een subblok van ~3 seconden, maar écht final is pas de summary van ~2 minuten?
2.  In de paper is een summary PoW-loos. Nexa maakt van het laatste subblok de summary. Verlies je daarmee niet juist het “iedere node plakt zelf de summary”-voordeel, of is dat juist slimmer tegen forks?
3.  Reward-korting op boomdiepte klinkt goed tegen selfish mining. Doet Nexa die korting 1-op-1 uit de paper, of alleen de DAG-structuur en Bobtail-variantie?
4.  Als subblokken in RAM leven en daarna getrimd worden: hoe bewijs ik over 5 jaar dat tx X in subblok Y zat? Blijft de summary genoeg voor een SPV-wallet?
5.  40 subblokken per summary, target 3 seconden. Wat gebeurt er als het netwerk even traag is en er 60 binnenkomen? Wie bepaalt welke 40 winnen — miner van de summary?
6.  Rolling checkpoints op 200 blokken: bij 2 minuten per summary is dat bijna 7 uur. Is dat niet laat voor exchanges, of juist de bedoeling zodat Tailstorm eerst mag reorgen?
7.  Hebben light wallets straks extra logic nodig, of zien ze gewoon dezelfde Nexa-keten en merken gebruikers niks tot de confirmatieteller sneller tikt?
8.  De paper straft withholding via diepte. Nexa telt uncles mee in het werk. Sluit dat elkaar niet een beetje uit? Uncle belonen = platte boom belonen?
messages.translation:
1. So if I understand correctly: my transaction will soon already be in a sub-block of ~3 seconds, but it's only truly final with the summary of ~2 minutes?
2. In the paper a summary is PoW-less. Nexa turns the last sub-block into the summary. Doesn't that lose exactly the "every node assembles the summary itself" advantage, or is that actually smarter against forks?
3. Reward discount based on tree depth sounds good against selfish mining. Does Nexa apply that discount one-to-one from the paper, or only the DAG structure and Bobtail variance?
4. If sub-blocks live in RAM and are then trimmed: how do I prove in 5 years that tx X was in sub-block Y? Does the summary remain enough for an SPV wallet?
5. 40 sub-blocks per summary, target 3 seconds. What happens if the network is slow for a bit and 60 come in? Who decides which 40 win — the miner of the summary?
6. Rolling checkpoints at 200 blocks: at 2 minutes per summary that's almost 7 hours. Isn't that late for exchanges, or is it precisely the intention so that Tailstorm is allowed to reorg first?
7. Will light wallets need extra logic soon, or do they just see the same Nexa chain and users notice nothing until the confirmation counter ticks faster?
8. The paper punishes withholding via depth. Nexa counts uncles towards the work. Don't those somewhat contradict each other? Rewarding uncles = rewarding a flat tree?
messages.note: These are pre-written suggested comments for supporters to post under the X article.

messages.text:
9.  Eindelijk iemand die uitlegt dat dit geen “we worden IOTA” is. Hybrid is het hele punt: DAG voor de pulse, keten voor de waarheid.
10.  2.2.0.0 als laatste checkpoint voelt precies goed. Consensus-code die “bijna klaar” is, moet je niet in een AMA live zetten.
11.  Die figuur met d=1 → r=1/3 is het hele incentive-verhaal in één plaatje. Delen loont, hameren op dezelfde ouder niet.
12.  Als miner: lagere variantie op 2 minuten is meer waard dan weer een nieuw ticker-verhaal. Pools haten lange staarten, solo-miners ook.
messages.translation:
9. Finally someone who explains that this isn't a "we're becoming IOTA" thing. Hybrid is the whole point: DAG for the pulse, chain for the truth.
10. 2.2.0.0 as the last checkpoint feels exactly right. Consensus code that's "almost done" shouldn't be pushed live during an AMA.
11. That figure with d=1 → r=1/3 is the whole incentive story in one picture. Sharing pays off, hammering on the same parent doesn't.
12. As a miner: lower variance over 2 minutes is worth more than yet another new ticker story. Pools hate long tails, and so do solo miners.

messages.text:
Hardwareversnelling: Schalen via circuits

In het tweede artikel van deze reeks werd de validatie-engine van Nexa opgebouwd uit zes componenten, een tape en een lees-/schrijfkop; vervolgens werd getoond hoe deze een betaling van Alice naar Bob afhandelde, volledig zonder tussenkomst van software.

Omdat de tape zich uitsluitend in voorwaartse richting bewoog, voldeed de engine aan het eerste van de vier criteria waaraan een verbeterde Bitcoin moet voldoen: hij was geschikt voor pipelining.

Dit artikel behandelt de resterende criteria. Zoals dr. Peter Rizun (@PeterRizun), Chief Scientist van Nexa, in Sydney aantoonde, kunnen we Satoshi's Bitcoin verbeteren en aan al deze eisen laten voldoen door slechts drie eenvoudige aanpassingen door te voeren. Daarbij krijgt de engine er – bijna gratis – nog twee eigenschappen bij: uitbreidbaarheid en comprimeerbaarheid.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749
messages.translation:
Hardware acceleration: Scaling via circuits

In the second article of this series, Nexa's validation engine was built up out of six components, a tape and a read/write head; it was then shown how this handled a payment from Alice to Bob, entirely without any software involvement.

Because the tape moved only in the forward direction, the engine met the first of the four criteria an improved Bitcoin must satisfy: it was suitable for pipelining.

This article covers the remaining criteria. As dr. Peter Rizun (@PeterRizun), Chief Scientist of Nexa, demonstrated in Sydney, we can improve Satoshi's Bitcoin and make it meet all these requirements by making just three simple changes. In doing so the engine gains — almost for free — two more properties: extensibility and compressibility.

https://forum.nexa.org/t/scaling-by-circuit/1749

summary.headline: Revived Dutch Nexa group talks Tailstorm hardfork, X-promotion tactics, price hopes and memecoin disdain
summary.summary: The Dutch/Belgian Nexa group was restarted about a week before this window and is picking up activity, with ZYDEXN welcoming returning member Jaxxx and a bot (Rose) greeting several new joiners. Lenn Treve drives the most substantive content: hype for the upcoming Tailstorm hybrid-DAG hardfork, a link to the arXiv paper, a Dutch-language explainer article on X, and a long list of prepared technical questions/comments (finality, sub-blocks, uncle rewards, checkpoints, SPV) plus a request for members to comment and copy-link the post within 30 minutes to game the algorithm. Price talk is bullish but vague — ZYDEXN and Lenn Treve speak of billions in market cap, a thin MEXC order book, and a push back to 0.00017. The one mild friction came when Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper pushed back on ZYDEXN also promoting $ALPH in a Nexa-focused channel; it was settled amicably, with ZYDEXN arguing cross-posting reaches a wider audience and agreeing the chat should stay Nexa-only. The window ends with playful talk about launching memes/tokens on Nexa via tokenex, dismissal of memecoins as gambling, and Lenn Treve speculating that an influencer is quietly accumulating Nexa.

topics.title: Tailstorm hardfork and technical deep-dive
topics.summary: Lenn Treve announced the upcoming Tailstorm hybrid-DAG hardfork, shared the arXiv paper and a Dutch explainer on X, and posted a detailed set of technical questions and talking points on sub-block finality, PoW-less summaries, uncle rewards, checkpoints and light wallets. Blacktea ▽ also shared a forum article on Peter Rizun's hardware-acceleration/'scaling by circuit' work.

topics.title: X promotion and algorithm boosting
topics.summary: Lenn Treve asked members to comment on and copy-link his article within 30 minutes for an algorithm boost, later reporting 'good quality accounts' engaging and that his new strategy works; ZYDEXN asked people to like and share his post too. Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper got excited that a serious account liked Lenn's post.

topics.title: ALPH cross-promotion friction
topics.summary: Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper gently objected to ZYDEXN promoting $ALPH alongside Nexa, saying the channel should stay Nexa-focused; ZYDEXN defended it as reaching a wider audience but agreed the chat should be purely Nexa, and both ended on friendly terms.

topics.title: Price and market cap expectations
topics.summary: ZYDEXN repeatedly predicted a 1B+ (and later multi-billion) market cap, noted the MEXC order book is very thin, and called for a push back to 0.00017; Lenn Treve agreed ATH would return once the masses catch on and later claimed Nexa was pumping while BTC and ETH stagnate.

topics.title: Memecoins vs building on Nexa
topics.summary: Lenn Treve and ZYDEXN dismissed memecoins as rug-prone gambling, then joked about launching a meme token on Nexa via tokenex — ZYDEXN suggesting a 'ZYDEXN coin' and Lenn Treve proposing the name SHITCOIN; Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper praised Nexa's fairness and its tooling for launching projects.

topics.title: Group revival and new members
topics.summary: Jaxxx returned and remarked the group had been dead; ZYDEXN explained it was relaunched a week ago and urged everyone to invite others. The Rose bot welcomed several newcomers and posted the standard exchange list with a self-custody reminder after a /buy command from Blacktea ▽.

topics.title: Community evangelism
topics.summary: Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper described himself as Nexa's biggest fan despite being called crazy, called for a 'Nexa movement' with street visibility and a Saylor-style 'Buy Nexa' sticker campaign, and argued Nexa can replace SOL, ETH and BTC.

summary.mood_description: The tone is upbeat throughout: a revived group, anticipation for the Tailstorm hardfork, and confident long-term price predictions. A brief dip into mild friction occurs when Sheldon ⛛ψ Cooper questions ZYDEXN's $ALPH posts, but it resolves politely within minutes. Late in the window the mood turns jokey (SHITCOIN, ZYDEXN coin) with only a small negative note about BTC and ETH stagnating.

highlights.why: Lenn Treve's eight detailed Tailstorm questions are the most substantive technical content in the window — finality, uncle rewards, checkpoints, SPV.
Explicit call to coordinate comments and copy-link clicks within 30 minutes for a '40x algorithm boost' — an organised engagement-farming request worth the team's attention.
The one moment of friction: a polite objection to $ALPH promotion in the Nexa channel, and the start of a short moderation-adjacent debate.
Lenn Treve's punchline after the memecoin-bashing: proposing to launch a Nexa token called SHITCOIN.
Concrete market observation — the MEXC order book is described as very thin, relevant context for the bullish price talk.
